title: Episode 74: C++ Education, Cats and More! 🐈‍⬛

sentences.en: I'll say this, you are not the oldest guest we've had on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我得说，你并不是我们播客请过的最年长的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're very sweet.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你人真好。

sentences.en: I just turned 50 in like a few weeks back.
sentences.zh: 我几周前刚满50岁。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're not even in like the top two or three of us guests.
sentences.zh: 没错，你甚至排不进我们嘉宾年龄的前两三名。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 74, recorded on April 14th, 2022.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听ADSP播客第74期，录制于2022年4月14日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we interview Patrice Roy about C++ education, cats, and more.
sentences.zh: 我是Connor，今天我和联合主持人Bryce一起采访Patrice Roy，聊聊C++教育、猫以及更多话题。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I was thinking about this the other day that I was thinking about the nature of programming books that I think,
sentences.zh: 前几天我还在思考编程书籍的本质，我想，

sentences.en: and maybe this is untrue, but I'll put out my theory here, which is I know a lot of people who write programming books.
sentences.zh: 也许这不对，但我还是想提出我的理论，因为我认识很多写编程书的人。

sentences.en: I have a shelf full of books that are written by my friends.
sentences.zh: 我的书架上摆满了朋友们写的书。

sentences.en: But my impression is that most of them are written with the audience of post-education people,
sentences.zh: 但我的印象是，大多数书的受众都是已经完成学业的人，

sentences.en: people that have graduated from college that are practicing, you know, software engineers or programmers
sentences.zh: 也就是那些大学毕业后正在从事软件工程或编程工作的从业者，

sentences.en: and who want to continue learning their skills, and that they're not written as textbooks.
sentences.zh: 他们希望继续提升技能，所以这些书并不是作为教科书编写的。

sentences.en: And I guess my impression is that like in other fields, that tends to be less the case.
sentences.zh: 我感觉在其他领域，情况似乎不太一样。

sentences.en: It tends to be more that books get written as, you know, explicitly as textbooks or as course books.
sentences.zh: 通常书籍更多是明确作为教科书或课程教材来编写的。

sentences.en: Maybe I'm wrong about that.
sentences.zh: 也许我对此有误解。

sentences.en: Maybe my perception is off here.
sentences.zh: 也许我的看法有偏差。

sentences.en: I certainly know that some of the C++ books that I'm familiar with are used as course textbooks.
sentences.zh: 我确实知道我熟悉的一些C++书籍被用作课程教材。

sentences.en: Maybe not at like the, you know, the introductory level, but at the higher levels.
sentences.zh: 可能不是在入门级别，但在更高阶的课程中是这样。

sentences.en: But I think it is sort of like an interesting phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一种有趣的现象。

sentences.en: It reminds me of another thing, which is when I was a kid, I would go to conferences all the time with my mother
sentences.zh: 这让我想起另一件事，小时候我经常跟着母亲去参加会议，

sentences.en: because she's a lawyer and lawyers have to do a certain amount of continuing education every year
sentences.zh: 因为她是律师，律师每年必须完成一定量的继续教育，

sentences.en: to keep up with their certifications, their, you know, their bar association memberships in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 以维持他们的认证资格，也就是在美国的律师协会会员资格。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the ways that you can qualify to do that for that continuing education is to go to a conference and, you know, attend some classes there,
sentences.zh: 你知道，获得继续教育学分的方法之一就是去参加会议，听一些课程，

sentences.en: which is a lot more fun than just like taking some training courses.
sentences.zh: 这比单纯参加培训课程要有趣得多。

sentences.en: So, of course, that's what we would do.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们当然会那样做。

sentences.en: But there's no real certification or requirement for that in, you know, the programming industry.
sentences.zh: 但在编程行业，并没有真正的认证或强制要求。

sentences.en: So, it's sort of up to our own, to each of us to feel motivated to continue learning.
sentences.zh: 所以，是否有动力继续学习，很大程度上取决于我们每个人自己。

sentences.en: Yeah, but if you don't, you're going to get stuck way, way back and you're going to stop following what's going on in the world.
sentences.zh: 没错，但如果你不学习，你就会远远落后，跟不上世界的发展。

sentences.en: And the, I don't use books written.
sentences.zh: 而且，我并不使用那些书。

sentences.en: I have probably the same books you have.
sentences.zh: 我可能和你拥有一样的书。

sentences.en: I don't use most of them in my classes.
sentences.zh: 我在课堂上并不使用它们中的大多数。

sentences.en: I do suggest chapters from time to time to students.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔会向学生推荐其中的章节。

sentences.en: I write my own material.
sentences.zh: 我自己编写教材。

sentences.en: If you look for introductory books, there's one from Bjarne that's kind of cool.
sentences.zh: 如果你在找入门书，Bjarne写的那本还不错。

sentences.en: The one with the birds on it.
sentences.zh: 就是封面上画着鸟的那本。

sentences.en: Yeah, the tour of C++.
sentences.zh: 对，《C++之旅》。

sentences.en: No, this is cool if you already know how to program.
sentences.zh: 不，如果你已经会编程了，那本很棒。

sentences.en: But the Programming Principles book with the swans on it, it's written for undergrads, so it's kind of accessible.
sentences.zh: 但那本封面上画着天鹅的《程序设计原理与实践》，是为本科生写的，所以比较容易上手。

sentences.en: And what I like about it is that it goes into detail as to why you do that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它的一点是，它深入讲解了为什么要那样做。

sentences.en: Oh, you can do things with the language, what the purpose is, what the, there are pictures of people like Stepanov and they're like,
sentences.zh: 哦，你可以用这门语言做各种事，它的目的是什么，还有像Stepanov这样的人的照片，他们就像是，

sentences.en: these are the artisans, the people that have worked on this.
sentences.zh: 这些人是工匠，是致力于此的人。

sentences.en: The language lives through them.
sentences.zh: 这门语言因他们而鲜活。

sentences.en: So there's, I think for beginners, it's an interesting book.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对于初学者来说，这是一本很有趣的书。

sentences.en: It's a bit big maybe for a class, but I don't use it.
sentences.zh: 对于课堂来说可能有点厚，但我不用它。

sentences.en: So the one that portrays, there's a few different books by Bjarne.
sentences.zh: 所以Bjarne写过几本不同的书。

sentences.en: And two of the more mainstream and popular ones are the swan book one, which is Programming Principles and Practices Using C++ by Bjarne.
sentences.zh: 其中两本比较主流和流行的是天鹅封面的那本，也就是Bjarne的《C++程序设计原理与实践》。

sentences.en: The other one, which is one that I, is perhaps the most frequently cited introductory C++ book that I know of, is the C++ Programming Language book,
sentences.zh: 另一本是我所知的引用频率最高的C++入门书，是《C++程序设计语言》，

sentences.en: which is, has a similar cover in that both covers are blue, but the C++ Programming Language book has mountains on it.
sentences.zh: 它的封面和那本很像，都是蓝色的，但《C++程序设计语言》封面上是山。

sentences.en: I don't know if there's a fifth edition of it now.
sentences.zh: 我不知道现在有没有第五版了。

sentences.en: The fourth edition was, I think, the C++ 11.
sentences.zh: 第四版我想是针对C++ 11的。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to write one because the language has changed too much.
sentences.zh: 他不想再写一本了，因为语言变化太大了。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's a good introductory book if you've never programmed before, though.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为如果你从未学过编程，它是一本好的入门书。

sentences.en: It's a good book to get C++ if you learn something else in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你过去学过其他语言，它是学习C++的好书。

sentences.en: Yeah, interesting.
sentences.zh: 是啊，很有趣。

sentences.en: I know some professors that have used it for an intro programming course that was taught in C++.
sentences.zh: 我知道有些教授在用C++教授的入门编程课上用过它。

sentences.en: There's some other books that Bjarne have written, like The Design and Evolution of C++.
sentences.zh: Bjarne还写过其他书，比如《C++语言的设计与演化》。

sentences.en: That's an awesome book.
sentences.zh: 那是一本很棒的书。

sentences.en: That's really, really, really good.
sentences.zh: 真的非常非常好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I recently was diving in it to find quotes for something.
sentences.zh: 我最近还在翻阅它，为了找一些引言。

sentences.en: It is a pretty solid book.
sentences.zh: 这是一本相当扎实的好书。

sentences.en: It gives you perspective as to why things are the way they are, why the model is what it is, and how it differs from other languages.
sentences.zh: 它让你从视角上理解为什么事物是现在的样子，为什么模型是这样的，以及它与其他语言有何不同。

sentences.en: So even if you don't like C++, you should read that book to at least get why the language is what it is.
sentences.zh: 所以即使你不喜欢C++，也应该读读那本书，至少能明白这门语言为何如此。

sentences.en: Because there's purpose to that.
sentences.zh: 因为这背后是有目的的。

sentences.en: There's meaning to that.
sentences.zh: 是有意义的。

sentences.en: I passed it along to my colleagues, and everybody loved it.
sentences.zh: 我把它推荐给了同事，大家都非常喜欢。

sentences.en: Even those who don't do C++, they love the book.
sentences.zh: 即使是不写C++的人，也喜欢这本书。

sentences.en: So you said you develop your own course material.
sentences.zh: 所以你说你开发自己的课程材料。

sentences.en: Is that pretty common in the CS world?
sentences.zh: 这在计算机科学界很常见吗？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know about the CS world entirely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不完全了解整个计算机科学界。

sentences.en: In where I work, many of us do that.
sentences.zh: 但在我工作的地方，我们很多人都这样做。

sentences.en: So it's, yeah, I'm a bit of a maniac for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我在这方面有点狂热。

sentences.en: So I write new stuff all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在写新的东西。

sentences.en: Now, of course, I'm going to put you on the spot.
sentences.zh: 现在，当然，我要让你当场回答一下。

sentences.en: Is it open source?
sentences.zh: 它是开源的吗？

sentences.en: Well, if you can read French, a lot of it is on my website.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你能读懂法语，很多内容都在我的网站上。

sentences.en: I have a very big website with awful colors, I know, but that's on purpose.
sentences.zh: 我有一个很大的网站，配色很糟糕，我知道，但那是故意的。

sentences.en: It's an ugly-looking site with lots of contents that people who speak French look at quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 这是一个外观丑陋但内容丰富的网站，讲法语的人经常看。

sentences.en: I used to have a password on the site, but it was a hassle because people couldn't reach it through Google.
sentences.zh: 我以前给网站设过密码，但很麻烦，因为人们无法通过谷歌搜索到它。

sentences.en: So I removed that.
sentences.zh: 所以我取消了密码。

sentences.en: But the course material that's in book format is accessible, but universities, they want to control access a bit.
sentences.zh: 但书本格式的课程材料是可以获取的，只是大学方面希望稍微控制一下访问权限。

sentences.en: So they're on mobile sites, so it's not as open source as it could be.
sentences.zh: 所以它们在移动端网站上，不像本可以做到的那样完全开源。

sentences.en: If I do a big update of everything at some point, now I don't have the time these days, I might just publish an article form on my site to make it available to more people.
sentences.zh: 如果哪天我有时间对所有内容进行大更新，我可能会直接以文章形式发布在网站上，让更多人能看到。

sentences.en: So right now, there's an overlap between the book stuff that I write that's for the students and the article stuff that I write that's on my site.
sentences.zh: 所以目前，我为学生编写的书籍内容和我发布在网站上的文章内容之间存在重叠。

sentences.en: In some cases, the site is more up-to-date.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，网站上的内容更新。

sentences.en: In some cases, the books are more up-to-date.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，书里的内容更新。

sentences.en: But the overall stuff is pretty good, I think.
sentences.zh: 但我认为整体内容还是相当不错的。

sentences.en: It seems to me like we in the software world, we know how to do open collaboration between different spanning organizations and national boundaries and everything.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，我们软件界的人懂得如何在跨组织、跨国界等各种情况下进行开放协作。

sentences.en: It seems like, you know, why doesn't like every programming language or every field in CS have like some, you know, open source collaborative effort to develop, you know,
sentences.zh: 看起来，你知道，为什么不是每种编程语言或计算机科学的每个领域都有某种，你知道，开源协作的努力来开发，你知道，

sentences.en: educational material for the university level?
sentences.zh: 大学水平的教育材料呢？

sentences.en: That's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: There are open classes.
sentences.zh: 确实有公开课。

sentences.en: Maybe it's just because schools make money out of that.
sentences.zh: 也许只是因为学校能从中赚钱。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It can be that simple.
sentences.zh: 可能就这么简单。

sentences.en: Why do we sell the standard on ISO?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要向ISO购买标准？

sentences.en: It's because there's some slight amount of money to be made out of it, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为这能赚点小钱吧。

sentences.en: I want people in my classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 我希望学生在我的教室里。

sentences.en: I want to be with people and talk to them.
sentences.zh: 我希望和人面对面交流。

sentences.en: So I don't want to record my classes and let people watch them from home using popcorn and beer.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想录制课程，让人们在家一边喝啤酒吃爆米花一边看。

sentences.en: I prefer them to be having popcorn and beer with me or something.
sentences.zh: 我更希望他们和我一起喝啤酒吃爆米花，或者类似的事情。

sentences.en: So if I publish everything online, I'm going to be alone in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我把所有东西都发布在网上，我就要独自坐在教室里了。

sentences.en: It's going to be boring.
sentences.zh: 那会很无聊。

sentences.en: I have that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我有这种感觉，是的。

sentences.en: So do you teach all your classes in French?
sentences.zh: 那你所有的课都是用法语教的吗？

sentences.en: No, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我教的。

sentences.en: The CP North class would be in English, of course.
sentences.zh: CP North的课程当然是用英语授课的。

sentences.en: I meant the university classes.
sentences.zh: 我是指大学课程。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Sometimes I give, when we have students from outside of Canada quite a bit, sometimes they do give bits in English.
sentences.zh: 有时，当有很多加拿大以外的学生时，有时确实会用英语讲一部分。

sentences.en: I answer English questions in English to help people along.
sentences.zh: 我会用英语回答英语问题，以帮助大家跟上进度。

sentences.en: But people who come to study with our class, in our classroom, they do have to learn French or speak French.
sentences.zh: 但那些来我们教室学习的学生，确实必须学习法语或会说法语。

sentences.en: There's a video game graduate class that we've been offering for 17 years now.
sentences.zh: 我们提供了一个电子游戏研究生课程，已经开设17年了。

sentences.en: It's a full-time graduate degree for people who want to come in and participate in game development.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全日制研究生学位，面向那些想要参与游戏开发的人。

sentences.en: In this class, there's a lot of French from France students, but there's also Spanish people.
sentences.zh: 在这个班里，有很多来自法国的学生，但也有西班牙人。

sentences.en: There's people from Eastern Europe, from South America, from the English-speaking world too.
sentences.zh: 还有来自东欧、南美以及英语世界的人。

sentences.en: But the classes are in French, so I graduate them as much as I can when they're stuck.
sentences.zh: 但课程是用法语讲的，所以当他们卡住时，我会尽可能地帮他们毕业。

sentences.en: But otherwise, well, they're learning and they're doing well.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，嗯，他们学得很好，表现也不错。

sentences.en: Anyway, they want to work in Montreal, so learning French is a plus.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们想在蒙特利尔工作，所以学会法语是一个加分项。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's important.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很重要。

sentences.en: So, are there any challenges to teaching something like C++ in French, C++, you know, the language, you know,
sentences.zh: 那么，用法语教授像C++这样的课程有什么挑战吗？C++，你知道，这门语言，你知道，

sentences.en: and the constructs of the language are obviously sort of very English-centric in nature.
sentences.zh: 语言的结构显然本质上是非常以英语为中心的。

sentences.en: Are there any, you know, challenges that come out of that?
sentences.zh: 这会带来什么挑战吗？

sentences.en: You want the funny ones?
sentences.zh: 你想听听有趣的吗？

sentences.en: Yes, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So, something like length, the T and the H, they're so hard to write for French-speaking people, they keep mixing them up.
sentences.zh: 比如“length”这个词，T和H，对讲法语的人来说太难写了，他们总是搞混。

sentences.en: But no, it's not that difficulty.
sentences.zh: 但不是，这并不是真正的困难。

sentences.en: Most people here in Montreal, they speak both languages.
sentences.zh: 蒙特利尔的大多数人都会说两种语言。

sentences.en: So, they kind of have the basics of English at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们至少有英语基础。

sentences.en: Coming from France, those who come from France, they do have some basics in English too, so they kind of get along.
sentences.zh: 来自法国的人，他们也有一些英语基础，所以他们能应付得来。

sentences.en: So, if you ask them to write a paper for you, it might be unpleasant to read because the syntax would be all wrong, but, you know, it's nothing that difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你让他们写论文，读起来可能不太舒服，因为语法可能全错，但你知道，这没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: The most difficult thing is getting people to structure their thought, and that's regardless of language.
sentences.zh: 最困难的是让人们理清思路，这与语言无关。

sentences.en: So, writing smaller functions, more focused classes, stop using pointers all over the place when you don't need them, things like that,
sentences.zh: 比如编写更小的函数、更专注的类、不要在不需要的地方到处使用指针等等，

sentences.en: and that has nothing to do with English or French.
sentences.zh: 这和英语或法语完全没关系。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting to think about, you know, people programming in languages other than English,
sentences.zh: 你知道，思考人们使用非英语语言编程很有趣，

sentences.en: because I'm not really aware of any programming languages where the constructs are not, or the keywords are not sort of very English-centric.
sentences.zh: 因为我真的不知道有什么编程语言的结构或关键字不是以英语为中心的。

sentences.en: There are some, there are some people in French.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些，有一些法语的。

sentences.en: It's very, very strange when you look at it, though I've seen that.
sentences.zh: 虽然我见过，但看起来非常非常奇怪。

sentences.en: There's APL, it was more math-oriented.
sentences.zh: 有APL，它更偏向数学。

sentences.en: And there's weird things, yeah.
sentences.zh: 还有一些奇怪的东西，是的。

sentences.en: There's weird things like white space where, you know, everything that you write, that's not a white space in the country.
sentences.zh: 还有像Whitespace这样奇怪的东西，你知道，你写的一切，只要不是空格，在那个国家里就不是空格。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But are there any languages where the keywords are not English keywords?
sentences.zh: 但有没有关键字不是英语的语言呢？

sentences.en: As I said, I know in dev that does that.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我知道有些开发环境是那样的。

sentences.en: I sometimes have people having internships in places where they use that, but it's kind of English, I'd say.
sentences.zh: 我有时会有实习生在那种环境的地方工作，但我会说，那本质上还是英语。

sentences.en: It's understandable if you think of it, because you want to reach a wider audience in the language of these days.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到这一点，这是可以理解的，因为你想用当今的语言去触及更广泛的受众。

sentences.en: So, if you're C-sharp, the guy who wrote that is Danish, but it's an English language, and Bjarne is from the Scandinavian countries too, but it's, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你用的是 C#，写那东西的人是丹麦人，但它是一门英语语言；Bjarne 也来自斯堪的纳维亚国家，但它，你知道，

sentences.en: your audience is English.
sentences.zh: 你的受众是讲英语的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And for a long time in a language like C++, you couldn't have non-ASCII identifiers, or even, you know, there were some compilers that would reject comments if they were not ASCII.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，像 C++ 这样的语言，你无法使用非 ASCII 标识符，甚至，你知道，有些编译器如果发现注释不是 ASCII 编码的，就会拒绝编译。

sentences.en: And if I may, I have so much respect for the SG16 people who aren't working on Unicode for C++.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我对那些致力于 C++ Unicode 标准的 SG16 成员怀有崇高的敬意。

sentences.en: My hat tip to them, they are heroes.
sentences.zh: 向他们致敬，他们是英雄。

sentences.en: Yeah, when is C++ going to get Unicode?
sentences.zh: 是啊，C++ 什么时候才能支持 Unicode？

sentences.en: I need to be able to write my APL compiler in C++, and I tell you, I tell you, trying to, like, iterate over a string that does not contain UTF-8 or the 256,
sentences.zh: 我需要能够用 C++ 编写我的 APL 编译器，我跟你说，我跟你说，尝试去遍历一个不包含 UTF-8 或 256 字符的字符串，

sentences.en: it is...
sentences.zh: 那简直是……

sentences.en: You should try Zach Lane's text library, which I think is part of Boost now.
sentences.zh: 你应该试试 Zach Lane 的文本库，我想它现在是 Boost 的一部分了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'll look into it.
sentences.zh: 我会去看看的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, do you know of any languages that have non-English keywords?
sentences.zh: 那么，你知道有什么语言使用非英语关键字吗？

sentences.en: I think we asked this question earlier on another podcast, and we had a response from someone on Twitter that said, oh, there is actually a language, and they linked me to it,
sentences.zh: 我想我们在之前的播客里问过这个问题，当时推特上有人回复说，哦，确实有这样一门语言，他们还给我发了链接，

sentences.en: but I do not have it top of mind.
sentences.zh: 但我现在想不起来了。

sentences.en: I'll throw a language out there that doesn't have non-English keywords, but it has a very interesting character set, and it's called Jelly.
sentences.zh: 我倒是可以提一门没有非英语关键字的语言，但它有一套非常有趣的字符集，它叫 Jelly。

sentences.en: I'll just leave that for the listener to go explore.
sentences.zh: 我就把这个留给听众自己去探索吧。

sentences.en: Just Google Jelly programming language.
sentences.zh: 直接谷歌搜索 Jelly 编程语言就行。

sentences.en: I've had to use tricks in jobs I've done in the past, in the recent past, that brought me to pre-C++ 98.
sentences.zh: 在过去，在最近的过去，我不得不使用一些技巧，这让我回到了 C++98 之前的时代。

sentences.en: And, you know, the toolbox, when you have a full toolbox, it's very, very useful in those moments.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当你拥有一个完整的工具箱时，在那些时刻它真的非常、非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can't imagine.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我无法想象。

sentences.en: I can't imagine.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象。

sentences.en: You know, C++11, that's what I started with, because I started working in C++, well, not in C++.
sentences.zh: 你知道，C++11 是我起步的版本，因为我开始使用 C++ 工作时，嗯，其实不是在 C++ 里。

sentences.en: I started working in the year 2014, and we were using C++11 at that point.
sentences.zh: 我是在 2014 年开始工作的，那时我们用的是 C++11。

sentences.en: I don't even think the full feature, because we had some Visual Studio 2000-something that only had like half of the features.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不觉得那是完整的功能，因为我们当时用的 Visual Studio 2000 某版本只实现了大概一半的功能。

sentences.en: Still, they had the auto-keyword and lambdas and stuff like that, and yeah, I can't imagine having to go back, and every time you want a callable,
sentences.zh: 不过，它们确实有 auto 关键字和 lambda 之类的东西，是的，我无法想象如果必须回到过去，每次想要一个可调用对象时，

sentences.en: you have to build a function object in the form of a struct with a, like, just there's so many things that, like, I took for granted when I started with the language.
sentences.zh: 都得构建一个结构体形式的函数对象，就像，我刚开始接触这门语言时，有太多东西是我视为理所当然的了。

sentences.en: And you'd hear about people being like, oh, you know, you don't know what it was like, and I'd be like, I don't know, it seems like a pretty nice language to me.
sentences.zh: 你会听到人们说，哦，你不知道过去是什么样子的，我会说，我不知道，对我来说它看起来是一门相当不错的语言。

sentences.en: But then you realize that there were the, I don't want to call them the dark ages, but just like the pre-C++11 ages.
sentences.zh: 但后来你意识到，确实存在过，我不想称之为黑暗时代，但确实存在过 C++11 之前的时代。

sentences.en: And so when you mentioned pre-C++98, that's, I can't even, yeah, I can't even imagine.
sentences.zh: 所以当你提到 C++98 之前时，我甚至，是的，我甚至无法想象。

sentences.en: It was a lot of fun, because it was an alien place where they had to certify the binaries that they were generating.
sentences.zh: 那真的很有趣，因为那是一个异类空间，他们必须对生成的二进制文件进行认证。

sentences.en: So they had to compile stuff in debug mode to make sure it was the readable binaries.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须在调试模式下编译代码，以确保二进制文件是可读的。

sentences.en: And then they certified them, and it cost so much that they didn't want to change the compilers in any way to make sure that the binaries were as stable as they could.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会对这些文件进行认证，成本太高了，以至于他们不想以任何方式更改编译器，以确保二进制文件尽可能稳定。

sentences.en: So we were using compilers I had not used in my 23 years of teaching.
sentences.zh: 所以我们使用的编译器甚至在我 23 年的教学生涯中都没用过。

sentences.en: It's older stuff than that.
sentences.zh: 那是更古老的东西。

sentences.en: So I had to really pick in my old toolbox.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的得在我的旧工具箱里翻找。

sentences.en: If you took a problem like doing function composition, f of g of x, and you try to solve the problem with C++98, 11, 14, 17, 20,
sentences.zh: 如果你拿一个像函数组合 f(g(x)) 这样的问题，尝试用 C++98、11、14、17、20 来解决，

sentences.en: the evolution of the way you solve that problem is amazing.
sentences.zh: 解决这个问题的方式的演变真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: It's gotten so simple and so clean and so efficient, and it used to be doable, but in such convoluted ways.
sentences.zh: 它变得如此简单、简洁且高效，以前虽然也能做到，但方式太复杂了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's a number of things we have learned over time, and the language is really helping us.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，随着时间的推移，我们学到了很多东西，这门语言确实在帮助我们。

sentences.en: So, yeah, we're going to solve problems in many different manners in that class, and I think it's going to be awesome.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在那门课上，我们将用许多不同的方式来解决问题，我认为这会非常棒。

sentences.en: So, Patrice, you haven't always been a professor, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，Patrice，你并不一直都是教授，对吧？

sentences.en: I thought you worked on some pretty cool stuff for your professor.
sentences.zh: 我记得你以前为你的教授做过一些很酷的项目。

sentences.en: Didn't you do, like, flight simulators or something?
sentences.zh: 你是不是做过飞行模拟器之类的东西？

sentences.en: Yeah, I did research for Hydro-Quebec, which is the biggest company in Quebec here.
sentences.zh: 是的，我为魁北克水电公司做过研究，那是我们魁北克最大的公司。

sentences.en: It's a state-owned thing where we produce electricity, and since we have a lot of water in Quebec, well, we have a lot of electricity.
sentences.zh: 那是一家国有企业，我们生产电力，而且因为魁北克水资源丰富，所以我们的电力非常充足。

sentences.en: And after that, I did a few years of military flight simulator work.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我做了几年军事飞行模拟器的工作。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So what do you want to know about that?
sentences.zh: 那么你想了解关于那方面的什么？

sentences.en: So was that all in C++?
sentences.zh: 那全是用 C++ 写的吗？

sentences.en: Was that in, like, C++ in the early C++ days?
sentences.zh: 是在 C++ 早期的时候吗？

sentences.en: Okay, so now you want the stories.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在你想听故事了。

sentences.en: When I got there, the reason I got into flight simulators at first was that I had gotten a scholarship for graduate studies, and I had a baby,
sentences.zh: 我刚到那里时，最初接触飞行模拟器的原因是，我当时拿到了研究生奖学金，而且我有了个孩子，

sentences.en: and another baby was coming along that was not expected.
sentences.zh: 还有一个意外到来的孩子。

sentences.en: And I looked at my scholarship and said, oh, we're going to have a problem.
sentences.zh: 我看了看我的奖学金，心想，哦，我们要有麻烦了。

sentences.en: Money is not going to be sufficient.
sentences.zh: 钱不够用了。

sentences.en: So I applied there because a friend told me, oh, we're looking for people.
sentences.zh: 所以我申请了那份工作，因为有个朋友告诉我，哦，他们正在招人。

sentences.en: I went there, and they asked me, do you want to do military work?
sentences.zh: 我去了那里，他们问我，你想做军事项目吗？

sentences.en: And I said, no, I don't, and they still hired me, and they offered me a job doing military flight simulators, and I thought about saying no,
sentences.zh: 我说，我不想，但他们还是录用了我，并提供了一份做军事飞行模拟器的工作，我曾想过拒绝，

sentences.en: and then I looked at the money and said, well, I have no choice.
sentences.zh: 但后来我看了看薪水，心想，好吧，我没得选。

sentences.en: But I really, really enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 但我真的、真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: I learned a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我学到了很多东西。

sentences.en: It was very instructive.
sentences.zh: 那非常有启发性。

sentences.en: It was a milestone in my personal development.
sentences.zh: 那是我个人发展的一个里程碑。

sentences.en: It was a very good learning experience.
sentences.zh: 那是一次非常好的学习经历。

sentences.en: Now, when I got there, my boss was a Fortran 77 expert, and he was, you might not be aware of that, but Fortran 77, you don't have local variables.
sentences.zh: 当时，我的老板是 Fortran 77 专家，他，你可能不知道，Fortran 77 是没有局部变量的。

sentences.en: Everything is static.
sentences.zh: 所有东西都是静态的。

sentences.en: So if you were trying to write recursive functions, you're going to have a lot of pleasure.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想写递归函数，你会“享受”到很多乐趣。

sentences.en: He was scared of using the stack for functions because there seemed to be, in his mind, a cost to the stack pointer being incremented and incremented in code.
sentences.zh: 他害怕在函数中使用栈，因为在他看来，代码中栈指针的递增是有开销的。

sentences.en: So they're just selling the fact that we had local variables was a fight.
sentences.zh: 所以仅仅是推销我们拥有局部变量这一事实，就是一场斗争。

sentences.en: So it was a mix for Fortran 77 and size NCC that we had to do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不得不进行 Fortran 77 和 C 的混合编程。

sentences.en: Now, I was a C++ aficionado back then already with the C++ I knew, which was much more limited than what I know today.
sentences.zh: 那时我已经是一个 C++ 爱好者了，尽管我当时掌握的 C++ 比现在有限得多。

sentences.en: So I had built a framework of macros to make my C code behave kind of like C++ with initialization and stuff, which generated a lot of code because it was,
sentences.zh: 所以我建立了一个宏框架，让我的 C 代码表现得像带有初始化功能的 C++，这生成了大量的代码，因为，

sentences.en: I tried to be as clean as I could.
sentences.zh: 我尽量让它保持简洁。

sentences.en: And I actually saw an error message when I was there that claimed that the function had gotten too big through macros and the compiler refused to optimize it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至在那里看到过一条错误信息，声称函数通过宏变得太大了，编译器拒绝优化它。

sentences.en: I had never seen that before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未见过这种情况。

sentences.en: There are too many lines and I refused to optimize your code to go to hell.
sentences.zh: 代码行数太多，我拒绝优化你的代码，去死吧。

sentences.en: Kind of sounded like that.
sentences.zh: 听起来差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so I did that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我就是那样做的。

sentences.en: I worked on mostly helicopters that went to R, but also did search and rescue.
sentences.zh: 我主要从事直升机模拟工作，但也做过搜救模拟。

sentences.en: I worked on communication channels and I worked on a system that simulated voice messages within the simulated helicopters.
sentences.zh: 我研究过通信频道，还研究过一个在模拟直升机内模拟语音消息的系统。

sentences.en: Voice is interesting because it's a real-time system.
sentences.zh: 语音很有趣，因为它是一个实时系统。

sentences.en: It's hard real-time.
sentences.zh: 它是硬实时系统。

sentences.en: The people in the helicopter, they have to be able to tune in to a radio and listen to, believe it or not, the weather.
sentences.zh: 直升机里的人必须能够调频到广播，听听，信不信由你，天气预报。

sentences.en: But that's very important for them because they don't see what they're doing and they're guided mostly because there's always like fog and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但这对他们来说非常重要，因为他们看不见自己在做什么，而且主要是靠引导飞行，因为总是有雾之类的东西。

sentences.en: And they want to go to such and such airport and they want to know what the weather is to actually do their approach properly and don't kill themselves or anything.
sentences.zh: 他们想去某个机场，他们需要知道天气情况，才能正确地进行进场着陆，而不至于出事故。

sentences.en: And the executive system that we had there, so it was a layered thing with, see it as a four-level tree.
sentences.zh: 我们当时使用的执行系统，是一个分层结构，你可以把它看作一个四层树状结构。

sentences.en: The topmost part was a critical band where things have to be done at every iteration of the system and that's life-saving stuff.
sentences.zh: 最顶层是一个关键频带，系统每次迭代都必须完成这些任务，这关乎生命安全。

sentences.en: And as you go along down the tree, things get less and less critical.
sentences.zh: 随着你沿着树向下走，任务就越来越不关键。

sentences.en: So, they might skip turns from time to time.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们有时可能会跳过一些轮次。

sentences.en: And I happened with the system to have pieces on each and every level of the system.
sentences.zh: 而我碰巧在系统的每一层都有代码片段。

sentences.en: So, I got the whole experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，我获得了完整的体验。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it was the biggest flight simulator in the world back then.
sentences.zh: 而且那是当时世界上规模最大的飞行模拟器。

sentences.en: So, by far.
sentences.zh: 遥遥领先。

sentences.en: So, it was seen as a research project, but our motto was at CAE, we can.
sentences.zh: 所以，它被视为一个研究项目，但我们在 CAE 的座右铭是“我们能行”。

sentences.en: So, we said yes to everything regardless of whether it made sense or not.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论是否合理，我们对所有事情都说“是”。

sentences.en: And I was given 50 hours to take this bit of Fortran code that worked on a single helicopter and make it work on a system of helicopters that behaved as a unit when sharing a world through many machines.
sentences.zh: 我被给了 50 个小时，要把这段在单架直升机上运行的 Fortran 代码，改造成能在多台机器共享世界时作为一个整体运行的直升机系统。

sentences.en: Pure parallel code.
sentences.zh: 纯并行代码。

sentences.en: It was a concurrency and shared memory and stuff, which, of course, made no sense.
sentences.zh: 涉及并发和共享内存之类的东西，当然，这完全没道理。

sentences.en: It took three hours to do.
sentences.zh: 这花了三个小时才做完。

sentences.en: So, it was three hours, three years.
sentences.zh: 所以，是三个小时，三年。

sentences.en: Three years to do instead of 50 hours.
sentences.zh: 花了三年时间才完成，而不是 50 个小时。

sentences.en: It was crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And if you want the inside story, when I saw this, I said, I'm never going to write that in Fortran 77.
sentences.zh: 如果你想听内幕，当我看到这个时，我说，我绝不会用 Fortran 77 写这个。

sentences.en: It makes no sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说毫无意义。

sentences.en: It's way too hard.
sentences.zh: 太难了。

sentences.en: So, I asked for budget to rewrite it in C because C++ was out of the question.
sentences.zh: 所以我申请了预算用 C 语言重写它，因为 C++ 是不可能的。

sentences.en: It was too scary.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了。

sentences.en: And they said, no, we don't have the money.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，我们没钱。

sentences.en: So, I went on my own at night and I wrote the whole thing in C on my own time.
sentences.zh: 所以我晚上自己加班，利用业余时间用 C 语言重写了整个系统。

sentences.en: And I committed it and told nobody for a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 我提交了代码，几周内没告诉任何人。

sentences.en: And when everybody saw that it worked, then I told them.
sentences.zh: 当大家看到它能运行后，我才告诉他们。

sentences.en: And everyone was relieved because nobody wanted to do that in Fortran anyway.
sentences.zh: 每个人都松了一口气，因为反正没人想用 Fortran 做那个。

sentences.en: But, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的。

sentences.en: What year was this?
sentences.zh: 这是哪一年？

sentences.en: When was this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么时候？

sentences.en: I was there between 1995 and 1998.
sentences.zh: 我在 1995 年到 1998 年之间在那里工作。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Those were really the early days of C++ and you were already using it, already familiar with it.
sentences.zh: 那真的是 C++ 的早期，你当时就已经在使用它，并且已经很熟悉它了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I started using C++ around 1993 or something.
sentences.zh: 我大约在 1993 年左右开始使用 C++。

sentences.en: I'm old, sorry.
sentences.zh: 我老了，抱歉。

sentences.en: I'll say this.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是。

sentences.en: You are not the oldest guest we've had on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 你并不是我们播客请过的最年长的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're very sweet.
sentences.zh: 你真贴心。

sentences.en: I just turned 50 like a few weeks back.
sentences.zh: 我几周前刚满 50 岁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're not even in like the top two or three of us.
sentences.zh: 你甚至排不进我们嘉宾年龄的前两三名。

sentences.en: You're very sweet.
sentences.zh: 你真贴心。

sentences.en: To be honest, I would have stayed at CE if I had not gotten a teaching opportunity, but I wanted to do teaching long term.
sentences.zh: 老实说，如果不是因为得到了教学机会，我可能会留在 CAE，但我一直想长期从事教学工作。

sentences.en: And when I got an offer, I said, well, if I don't do it right now, I might never do it.
sentences.zh: 当我收到录用通知时，我想，如果我现在不去做，可能永远都不会去做了。

sentences.en: So, let's just do the move.
sentences.zh: 所以，就迈出这一步吧。

sentences.en: It cost me a lot of money to do that because I was well paid at CE.
sentences.zh: 这让我损失了很多钱，因为我在 CAE 的薪水很高。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, how many kids do you have now, Patrice?
sentences.zh: 那么，Patrice，你现在有几个孩子？

sentences.en: You mentioned two.
sentences.zh: 你提到了两个。

sentences.en: I can hear some kittens in the background.
sentences.zh: 我能听到背景里有小猫的声音。

sentences.en: I was really hoping we'd get to see one.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我们能看到一只。

sentences.en: No, they're sleeping right now.
sentences.zh: 不，它们现在在睡觉。

sentences.en: Most of them, I just fed them like 15 minutes ago.
sentences.zh: 大部分都在睡，我 15 分钟前刚喂过它们。

sentences.en: Someone had some cats or something that was going, meow.
sentences.zh: 刚才有人养了猫之类的，一直在叫，喵。

sentences.en: And I'll keep that in.
sentences.zh: 我会把这段保留下来。

sentences.en: I'll keep that in.
sentences.zh: 我会保留下来的。

sentences.en: Everyone's going to get to hear Connor as a cat.
sentences.zh: 每个人都能听到 Connor 像猫一样叫了。

sentences.en: I do know you have a lot of pets though, Patrice.
sentences.zh: 不过我知道你养了很多宠物，Patrice。

sentences.en: There are seven cats at home.
sentences.zh: 家里有七只猫。

sentences.en: There's one dog, three parrots, a hamster.
sentences.zh: 还有一只狗、三只鹦鹉和一只仓鼠。

sentences.en: The number of cats has gone up to as high as 30 from the region.
sentences.zh: 猫的数量一度从该地区增加到了30只。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But we have a shelter.
sentences.zh: 但我们有个收容所。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I was about to say, like, you basically have a farm or a shelter.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，你这基本上就是个农场或者收容所了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I have a wife who works at a veterinarian's clinic.
sentences.zh: 其实，我妻子在一家兽医诊所工作。

sentences.en: She's an expert in cat and dog nutrition.
sentences.zh: 她是猫狗营养方面的专家。

sentences.en: So, she works from home mostly and she guides people with probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以她大部分时间都在家办公，为遇到问题的宠物主人提供指导。

sentences.en: It's a free service.
sentences.zh: 这是项免费服务。

sentences.en: Some people just call that in or the scheduled meeting with her and they have an hour and she listens to what kind of problem they have.
sentences.zh: 有些人会打电话咨询，或者预约和她面谈，他们有一小时的时间，她会倾听他们遇到的各种问题。

sentences.en: And she guides them through their nutritionary needs.
sentences.zh: 然后她会根据宠物的营养需求给出建议。

sentences.en: And we have seven cats of our home.
sentences.zh: 我们自己家里养了七只猫。

sentences.en: They're all kind of weird, like with weird paws or weird defects.
sentences.zh: 它们都有点奇怪，比如爪子长得怪怪的，或者有些先天缺陷。

sentences.en: One of them is missing a tail, whatever.
sentences.zh: 其中一只没有尾巴，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And we take – in Quebec, most people move around July.
sentences.zh: 在魁北克，大多数人会在七月左右搬家。

sentences.en: There's a tradition where first of July, everyone's moving.
sentences.zh: 有个传统是七月一日大家都会搬家。

sentences.en: And people tend to abandon their cats around that time, which is very sad.
sentences.zh: 人们往往会在那个时候遗弃猫咪，这非常令人难过。

sentences.en: And when we were living, our previous house was about 15 minutes drive from where I live now.
sentences.zh: 我们以前住的地方离我现在住的地方大约有15分钟车程。

sentences.en: And my wife was in the – she was managing kind of a shelter organization where they rescued cats, sterilized them, vaccinated them, and let them go.
sentences.zh: 当时我妻子在管理一个收容组织，他们负责救助猫咪，给它们绝育、接种疫苗，然后再放归。

sentences.en: So, when they got pregnant cats, it was more complicated because you don't want to sterilize them with the babies in.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他们接到怀孕的母猫时，情况就比较复杂了，因为你不能给怀着小猫的母猫做绝育。

sentences.en: So, we used to take the cats down, let them have the babies, and then sterilize everyone and vaccinate everyone and find homes for them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们过去常把猫带回家，让它们生下小猫，然后再给所有猫做绝育、接种疫苗，并为它们找领养家庭。

sentences.en: So, we kept on doing that when we moved.
sentences.zh: 搬家后我们一直坚持这样做。

sentences.en: So, that's why sometimes we have as high as 30 cats because there was one time two years ago, three years ago,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有时候我们的猫会多达30只，因为两三年前有一次，

sentences.en: when we had four pregnant cat ladies in the span of a month, and all of them gave birth to four to six kittens.
sentences.zh: 在一个月内我们接纳了四只怀孕的母猫，它们每只都生了四到六只小猫。

sentences.en: So, they each had their own room, so they didn't fight.
sentences.zh: 所以它们每只都有自己的房间，这样就不会打架。

sentences.en: And there were seven little boxes to be twice a day.
sentences.zh: 而且每天要清理七个猫砂盆两次。

sentences.en: So, if I understand correctly, then it is likely that you will – that right before C++ North,
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，那么很有可能在C++ North大会之前，

sentences.en: you will have additional cats that will end up in the house because everybody's moving in July.
sentences.zh: 你们家里又会多出一些猫，因为大家都在七月搬家。

sentences.en: It's absolutely probable.
sentences.zh: 这绝对很有可能。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the kind of thing that tends to happen.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这种事确实常发生。

sentences.en: It's happened less with COVID because people moved less.
sentences.zh: 新冠期间这种情况少了一些，因为人们搬家少了。

sentences.en: But, yes, we do that.
sentences.zh: 但没错，我们确实会这样做。

sentences.en: And then, why do we do that?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们为什么要这么做呢？

sentences.en: Because we can.
sentences.zh: 因为我们有能力。

sentences.en: I mean, my wife is good at this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我妻子很擅长这个。

sentences.en: We can – when they need special medication or treatment, we can actually do that.
sentences.zh: 当它们需要特殊药物或治疗时，我们确实能做到。

sentences.en: We can prepare milk and feed them when the ladies cannot do that with small –
sentences.zh: 当猫妈妈无法照顾小猫时，我们可以准备奶水喂养它们——

sentences.en: I don't know what the English word for that is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道那个词的英文怎么说。

sentences.en: But, you know, when you feed babies with bottles, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，就是用奶瓶喂小宝宝，对吧。

sentences.en: So, we can do that with cats.
sentences.zh: 所以我们能用同样的方式照顾小猫。

sentences.en: They're very tiny bottles.
sentences.zh: 那是很小的奶瓶。

sentences.en: And when the lady cats cannot do it because already they kind of lick the babies to make them pee and stuff, well, you need to do it yourself.
sentences.zh: 当猫妈妈无法照顾时，因为它们通常会舔小猫来刺激它们排泄之类的，你就得自己动手了。

sentences.en: You need to put the baby cats on top of the sink or the toilet.
sentences.zh: 你需要把小猫放在水槽或马桶上。

sentences.en: You need to message them properly such that they pee and stuff.
sentences.zh: 你需要适当地按摩它们，让它们排泄之类的。

sentences.en: And then, you wash your hands, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，事后你得洗手。

sentences.en: So, I do that quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常做这些事。

sentences.en: How – do you put pictures of these cats in your talks?
sentences.zh: 你会把这些猫的照片放进你的演讲里吗？

sentences.en: You have to start if you don't.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没放，那你得开始了。

sentences.en: I've done that once or twice with a few cats.
sentences.zh: 我曾经放过一两次，用了几只猫的照片。

sentences.en: My wife has a Facebook account.
sentences.zh: 我妻子有Facebook账号。

sentences.en: She's more of a picture person than I am.
sentences.zh: 她比我更喜欢拍照。

sentences.en: But I've done that.
sentences.zh: 但我确实放过。

sentences.en: I'm not a big picture person.
sentences.zh: 我不是那种特别喜欢拍照的人。

sentences.en: But I have done talks with pictures of cats.
sentences.zh: 但我确实做过带猫咪照片的演讲。

sentences.en: But I feel – it feels weird to me to advertise that during my talks.
sentences.zh: 只是我觉得在演讲中宣传这些有点奇怪。

sentences.en: But I do talk about them.
sentences.zh: 但我确实会提到它们。

sentences.en: And you talked about the kids.
sentences.zh: 你还提到了孩子们。

sentences.en: I have five.
sentences.zh: 我有五个孩子。

sentences.en: There are only two left at home because theirs are all gone.
sentences.zh: 现在家里只剩下两个了，因为其他的都搬走了。

sentences.en: One of them is going to be a kind of lawyer soon.
sentences.zh: 其中一个快要成为律师了。

sentences.en: One of them is a dance instructor.
sentences.zh: 一个是舞蹈教练。

sentences.en: One of them is a literature major.
sentences.zh: 一个是文学专业的学生。

sentences.en: And I have a teenager and a young kid who's still in elementary school.
sentences.zh: 还有一个是十几岁的孩子，以及一个还在上小学的孩子。

sentences.en: And you teach it to different schools.
sentences.zh: 你还在不同的学校教书。

sentences.en: And I have a PhD, which I did along the way.
sentences.zh: 我还有一个博士学位，是在工作期间拿到的。

sentences.en: And I used to be a union worker, too, because I used to be part of the teachers' union.
sentences.zh: 我以前还是工会成员，因为我曾是教师工会的一员。

sentences.en: Well, one of the exigitive members.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是执行委员会成员之一。

sentences.en: And I do work now.
sentences.zh: 我现在还在工作。

sentences.en: What's the secret, Patrice?
sentences.zh: 秘诀是什么，Patrice？

sentences.en: Ask Bryce.
sentences.zh: 去问Bryce。

sentences.en: He never sleeps.
sentences.zh: 他从不睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, I do sleep from practice.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我确实会睡觉。

sentences.en: Bryce doesn't sleep, so.
sentences.zh: Bryce不睡觉，所以。

sentences.en: No, I had to take that out of my profile signature because now I sleep.
sentences.zh: 不，我不得不把那句话从我的个人签名里删掉了，因为我现在睡觉了。

sentences.en: My email signature for many years said sleep is for the week.
sentences.zh: 我的电子邮件签名多年来一直写着“睡觉是留给弱者的”。

sentences.en: But now that I'm an old man, I go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 但现在我老了，我会去睡觉。

sentences.en: What do I do?
sentences.zh: 我做什么？

sentences.en: When I feel tired, I go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 当我感到累的时候，我就去睡觉。

sentences.en: I can tell you that.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你这一点。

sentences.en: And since I've seen Michael Wong's resume, I don't feel like I work a lot anymore.
sentences.zh: 自从我看了Michael Wong的简历后，我就觉得我没那么忙了。

sentences.en: Because Michael is ridiculously busy.
sentences.zh: 因为Michael忙得离谱。

sentences.en: It makes no sense.
sentences.zh: 这简直没道理。

sentences.en: I don't know why he does it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他为什么这么拼。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I get up early.
sentences.zh: 不过，是的，我起得很早。

sentences.en: I go to bed late.
sentences.zh: 我睡得很晚。

sentences.en: And I try to do a proper job.
sentences.zh: 我努力把工作做好。

sentences.en: So that's what I do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所做的。

sentences.en: You know what's the most difficult these days?
sentences.zh: 你知道现在最困难的是什么吗？

sentences.en: There's been a lowering in literacy skills.
sentences.zh: 读写能力有所下降。

sentences.en: So people learning to make meaning out of the text that they read.
sentences.zh: 也就是人们理解所读文本含义的能力。

sentences.en: So in university, in college these days, what I noticed for the last two or three years, you have to repeat more what you say because people, they can read out loud the words,
sentences.zh: 所以在大学里，我注意到过去两三年里，你必须更多地重复你说过的话，因为人们虽然能大声读出单词，

sentences.en: but the phrases don't make the same sense to them as they do.
sentences.zh: 但句子对他们来说并没有传达出应有的意思。

sentences.en: So the thing I say the most these days is please reread the directives to make sure you've got them right.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在说得最多的一句话就是：请重读指令，确保你理解正确。

sentences.en: Please mark down what you've done because you probably didn't get it properly.
sentences.zh: 请标记出你所做的工作，因为你很可能没弄对。

sentences.en: And sometimes they give me homework back and I have to give back saying, that's not why I asked.
sentences.zh: 有时他们交回作业，我不得不退回去说，这不是我要求的。

sentences.en: Please do it again.
sentences.zh: 请重做一遍。

sentences.en: And when at some point I sat down with them and I've done that many times in the last few weeks, I read out loud with them the words and said, I never saw that paragraph.
sentences.zh: 当我有几次坐下来和他们一起逐字朗读时，我说，我从没见过那个段落。

sentences.en: It's the first one in the actual text.
sentences.zh: 它明明就在正文的第一段。

sentences.en: But they just came over.
sentences.zh: 但他们就是直接跳过了。

sentences.en: You don't see it.
sentences.zh: 他们看不见。

sentences.en: So my fight these days is make sure that you read because there's been a lowering during COVID times of reading skills.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在的抗争就是确保他们能阅读，因为在新冠期间，阅读能力确实有所下降。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I was just about to ask.
sentences.zh: 我正想问这个。

sentences.en: You said the last one to two years.
sentences.zh: 你说是一到两年内。

sentences.en: Do you think that that's related to the move to online?
sentences.zh: 你认为这和转向线上教学有关吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure there's an impact because it didn't used to be.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定有影响，因为以前不是这样的。

sentences.en: There's always people having problems with their reading skills, but to generalize like that, it's almost half of the students these days.
sentences.zh: 一直都有人阅读能力有问题，但像现在这样普遍，几乎有一半的学生都是如此。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 很有趣。

sentences.en: I used to have to, at the top of my exams, I would write RTQ, which stood for read the question.
sentences.zh: 我以前在考试卷头会写上RTQ，意思是“阅读题目”。

sentences.en: And this is not necessarily because I have a low proficiency in reading.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是因为我阅读能力差。

sentences.en: Like I read quite a bit, but especially with math exams, I get very, very excited because I know, like I see the structure of the problem in a few numbers.
sentences.zh: 我读得不少，但特别是在数学考试中，我很容易兴奋，因为我知道，我一眼就能看出问题的结构。

sentences.en: And I just assume, oh, I know, I know what to do here.
sentences.zh: 然后我就想，哦，我知道该怎么做了。

sentences.en: And then I'll end up, you know, there's times where I failed tests because I didn't actually read what it was asking me to do.
sentences.zh: 结果我有时会因为没真正读懂题目要求而挂科。

sentences.en: And I just sort of very quickly got excited, went ahead and answered.
sentences.zh: 我只是很快地兴奋起来，然后直接开始答题。

sentences.en: And then I got back and it would say, you know, 40%.
sentences.zh: 最后拿到成绩单，上面写着40%。

sentences.en: And I'd be like, what, what happened?
sentences.zh: 我会想，什么？发生了什么？

sentences.en: I like, I nailed that.
sentences.zh: 我明明答得很好啊。

sentences.en: And then I would go back and the commentary from the prof or the teacher would be like, this is not what, you know, was requested.
sentences.zh: 然后我回去看教授或老师的评语，他们会说，这根本不是题目要求的。

sentences.en: You know, please read more carefully.
sentences.zh: 你知道，请更仔细地阅读。

sentences.en: And yeah, that's, that's sometimes there's this interesting phenomenon that sometimes people that have a high reading proficiency and who can read very quickly will have trouble,
sentences.zh: 是的，有时会出现这种有趣的现象，即阅读能力强、阅读速度快的人反而会遇到困难，

sentences.en: like recognizing an error in a text.
sentences.zh: 比如识别不出文本中的错误。

sentences.en: Because they read through it so quickly that they like, you know, they, they, they just complete their mind, their head just like corrects whatever the error was in the sentence.
sentences.zh: 因为他们读得太快了，大脑会自动补全并修正句子中的错误。

sentences.en: And sorry about that.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you'll allow me, we used to, me and one of my close colleagues, we used to have this exam we passed to first year students,
sentences.zh: 如果允许的话，我和我的一位亲密同事过去常给大一学生出一道题，

sentences.en: like midway through the semester where there were objective questions.
sentences.zh: 在学期中途会有客观题。

sentences.en: So you have a choice of answers.
sentences.zh: 你有几个选项可选。

sentences.en: And in one of them, the answer was pseudocode.
sentences.zh: 其中一个选项的答案是“伪代码”（pseudocode）。

sentences.en: And, but we put pseudopod, P-O-D instead of code, which is a tentacle as for a sensor and pseudocode was the fourth one.
sentences.zh: 但我们写成了“伪足”（pseudopod），把code改成了pod，那是触手的意思，而伪代码是第四个选项。

sentences.en: And the only ones that missed it were the good students because they read too quickly.
sentences.zh: 唯一选错的就是那些好学生，因为他们读得太快了。

sentences.en: So they saw the first word and I used to give them, I used to draw small squids and end them over in the class in public saying, you got a prize today because you read too quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们只看到了第一个词，我以前会画些小乌贼发给班里的学生，公开说，今天你得奖了，因为你读得太快了。

sentences.en: So yeah, you only hit the bad word, the good students with that.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，这只会坑到那些好学生。

sentences.en: And it's funny.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: My dad would always joke to me, like when I was in high school and if I did poorly on something, he'd ask me and I'd say, ah, I didn't do that good.
sentences.zh: 我父亲总是跟我开玩笑，高中时如果我考得不好，他会问我，我会说，啊，我没考好。

sentences.en: But I mean, that's just because I didn't read the question correctly or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但那只是因为我没读懂题目之类的。

sentences.en: And, you know, so I knew what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 所以其实我知道我在做什么。

sentences.en: I just didn't.
sentences.zh: 只是没读对。

sentences.en: And it went on into university and like, whenever I would talk to him on the phone, he would just like, he just sort of chuckle because like, it's his joke is like, oh,
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续到大学，每当我在电话里跟他谈起时，他就会轻笑，因为他的笑话就是，哦，

sentences.en: you didn't read the question.
sentences.zh: 你没读题目。

sentences.en: Oh, surprise, surprise.
sentences.zh: 哦，不出所料。

sentences.en: You know that you did the only reason you did poorly is not because you didn't prepare.
sentences.zh: 你知道你考得不好的唯一原因不是因为没准备，

sentences.en: It's because you don't have time to like do the most important thing, which is to figure out what the test or the class is asking from you.
sentences.zh: 而是因为你没时间去做最重要的事情，那就是弄清楚考试或课程到底在要求你做什么。

sentences.en: At the level where we are, it's reading your messages.
sentences.zh: 在我们这个层面，就是阅读你的信息。

sentences.en: Professionals, they don't use well enough, but they're often quite talkative, you know, so when you read them properly, you kind of grasp the gist of what's missing.
sentences.zh: 专业人士写得不够好，但他们通常很健谈，所以当你仔细阅读时，你就能抓住缺失的要点。

sentences.en: You work your way through.
sentences.zh: 然后你就能迎刃而解了。

sentences.en: So getting them learn to read their messages is a fight because after two years in school, they still don't do it.
sentences.zh: 所以让他们学会阅读报错信息是一场苦战，因为即使在学校学了两年，他们还是不看。

sentences.en: So what's super, super interesting about that is a lot of the times in a production code base, you'll get some crazy template, you know, template metaprogramming, you know,
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，超级、超级有趣的地方在于，很多时候在生产代码库中，你会遇到一些疯狂的模板，你知道，模板元编程，你知道，

sentences.en: a hundred lines.
sentences.zh: 一百行代码。

sentences.en: Everyone's seen it.
sentences.zh: 大家都见过。

sentences.en: And my gut reaction is like, I don't know what this is doing.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应是，我根本不知道这玩意儿在干什么。

sentences.en: And then I'll go to Godbolt, I'll get some minimal, you know, reproducing version of it and it'll be the same sort of error.
sentences.zh: 然后我会去 Godbolt，弄出一个最小化的、可复现的版本，结果报错信息竟然是一样的。

sentences.en: But like now, because it's a minimal, you know, reproduce and like, I know exactly what's happening.
sentences.zh: 但现在，因为它是最小化的、可复现的，我完全清楚发生了什么。

sentences.en: I'll just read it and it'll actually tell me like in the midst of all the garbage, like the exact problem, which the previous error actually also said.
sentences.zh: 我读一下它，它实际上会在那一堆垃圾信息中告诉我确切的问题所在，而之前的报错其实也说了同样的话。

sentences.en: I just, I just like, I saw it and my eyes glazed over and I was like, oh, I'll go fix this in Godbolt.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我只是看了一眼，眼睛就花了，然后我想，哦，我还是去 Godbolt 修吧。

sentences.en: But like, it's like you said, a lot of the times the error messages, like in the midst of all the angle brackets, there is actually like very specifically what your issue is.
sentences.zh: 但就像你说的，很多时候报错信息，在那些尖括号的海洋里，其实非常具体地指出了你的问题所在。

sentences.en: If you had just taken the time to read it, which I rarely do, I just go to Godbolt.
sentences.zh: 如果你当时花点时间去读一下——虽然我很少这么做，我只会去 Godbolt——你就能看懂。

sentences.en: So there's something there that like, you know, we, we always complain about how awful they are,
sentences.zh: 所以这里有个问题，你知道，我们总是抱怨报错信息有多烂，

sentences.en: but like a lot of the times in the midst of that awfulness is actually like the key to the problem.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，在那堆烂摊子中间，其实藏着解决问题的关键。

sentences.en: We just don't.
sentences.zh: 我们只是没去读而已。

sentences.en: You're making a point for writing smaller functions and smaller meta functions.
sentences.zh: 你这是在强调编写更小的函数和更小的元函数的重要性。

sentences.en: And if you write small things, it's so much easier to find your way around.
sentences.zh: 如果你写的东西很小，找起问题来就容易多了。

sentences.en: You almost don't debug if you don't do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你不这样做，你几乎就没法调试。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, one thing that I, I've run into that a lot too, Connor, and I do the same thing where if it's, if it's looks like it's going to be hard,
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一件事我也经常遇到，Connor，我也做同样的事，如果看起来很难处理，

sentences.en: I'll just go to Godbolt to try to reproduce it there.
sentences.zh: 我就会去 Godbolt 尝试复现它。

sentences.en: Especially a lot of the bugs, because I mostly work in compilers these days.
sentences.zh: 尤其是很多 Bug，因为我最近主要在做编译器相关的工作。

sentences.en: A lot of the problems that I run into are bugs that are actually in the compiler.
sentences.zh: 我遇到的很多问题其实都是编译器本身的 Bug。

sentences.en: And so if it's a compiler, if I think it's a compiler bug, my first reaction is to reduce it down to, you know, the form that a compiler writer wants it in, which is, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果是编译器问题，如果我觉得这是个编译器 Bug，我的第一反应是把它简化成编译器开发者想要的那种形式，也就是，你知道，

sentences.en: purely like ideally pre-processed source code.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下是纯粹的预处理后的源代码。

sentences.en: That's like minimized that has no includes or anything so that it's, you know, an easy test input to reproduce.
sentences.zh: 那种经过最小化处理，没有 include 或其他杂项，方便作为测试输入的代码。

sentences.en: But one thing that I've often done with more complex template errors is I'll dump the error message to a text file.
sentences.zh: 但我处理复杂的模板错误时经常做的一件事，是把报错信息导出到文本文件里。

sentences.en: And then that lets me go and do some reformatting of it.
sentences.zh: 然后我就可以对它进行重新格式化。

sentences.en: If it's an error message where it's, it's complaining about like, you know, the second argument, the template argument in like a template that has like four or five arguments.
sentences.zh: 如果报错信息是在抱怨，比如，你知道，一个有四五个参数的模板里的第二个参数，

sentences.en: And like, maybe one of them's like, you know, just a string of like nonsense, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且其中一个参数可能是一长串乱七八糟的东西，你知道，

sentences.en: the default way that most compilers format that is just to give it to you all as one long line.
sentences.zh: 大多数编译器默认的格式化方式就是把它全堆在一行里给你。

sentences.en: And so oftentimes, if I take it into a text editor, and I just like start manipulating it, like put each argument on one line, then it becomes a lot easier for me to figure out,
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候，如果我把它放到文本编辑器里，开始手动调整，比如把每个参数换行显示，我就很容易弄清楚，

sentences.en: oh, this is actually what the problem was.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来问题出在这里。

sentences.en: You're making a point for indentation of code too, is the same thing.
sentences.zh: 你这也是在为代码缩进做辩护，道理是一样的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: On the other hand, some of the other compilers I work with, they try to do that sort of formatting for you in their error messages.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我使用的其他一些编译器，它们会尝试在报错信息中为你做这种格式化。

sentences.en: And it's like, it's hard to identify what the optimal formatting of an error message is going to be for like in the generic case.
sentences.zh: 但很难确定对于一般情况来说，什么样的报错信息格式才是最优的。

sentences.en: And so I think oftentimes it's good for us as programmers to take the error diagnostic and then like,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，作为程序员，我们拿到报错诊断信息后，

sentences.en: see if we can sort it into something that's a little bit more manageable ourselves.
sentences.zh: 自己试着把它整理得更易读一点，往往是件好事。

sentences.en: I think there's a tool that Vittorio Romeo has written, but I do not recall the name of, but it actually is like, you pipe your compilation into this,
sentences.zh: 我想 Vittorio Romeo 写过一个工具，我不记得名字了，但它确实能让你把编译输出通过管道传给它，

sentences.en: and then you can set the level of like nesting of the brackets that it shows.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以设置它显示的括号嵌套层级。

sentences.en: So by default, it like collapses all of it.
sentences.zh: 默认情况下，它会折叠所有内容。

sentences.en: And then you get like a much more succinct and like the idea is you can keep running it and increasing the level until the message that you, or the info that you need is there,
sentences.zh: 然后你会得到一个简洁得多的信息，思路就是你可以不断运行并增加层级，直到你需要的信息出现为止，

sentences.en: which is kind of a neat idea.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个很棒的点子。

sentences.en: One interesting problem that we have in the C++ space is the question of when you dump out an error that's got some sort of stack to it, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们在 C++ 领域遇到的一个有趣的问题是，当你输出带有某种堆栈信息的错误时，你知道，

sentences.en: like template instantiation stack, you know, which direction do you output?
sentences.zh: 比如模板实例化堆栈，你知道，你应该按什么方向输出？

sentences.en: Most compilers output from like the original source of the error all the way down to where it was triggered from.
sentences.zh: 大多数编译器是从错误的原始触发点一直输出到它被调用的地方。

sentences.en: And I think that's actually not very helpful because like you, you see, then when you get this long error dump, the last thing is going to be the first thing that you see.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这其实不太有用，因为当你看到这一长串错误转储时，最后的部分反而是你最先看到的。

sentences.en: The last part of the error must be the first thing you see.
sentences.zh: 错误的最后一部分必须是你最先看到的内容。

sentences.en: And if you see instantiated from here within main, you know, the place where it was instantiated from is maybe not the most helpful thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到的是“在 main 函数中实例化自此处”，你知道，实例化的地方可能并不是最有用的信息。

sentences.en: Oftentimes the most helpful thing is what the, the root of that, of that tree of this was the error that happened.
sentences.zh: 通常最有用的信息是那个错误树的根源，也就是到底发生了什么错误。

sentences.en: Um, I think the only compiler I've seen that does it the inverse direction, if I recall correctly is I think circle does it the other way around, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，据我所知，我见过唯一一个反向输出的编译器好像是 Circle，它是反着来的，嗯，

sentences.en: which I have found to be quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常有趣。

sentences.en: I'd love to see that be a switch for which direct, which, which, uh, you know, to reverse the template instantiate the, the error instantiation, like message order.
sentences.zh: 我很想看到一个开关，可以控制模板实例化错误信息的输出方向。

sentences.en: I'd love to see a switch for that so that I could, I would probably switch it by default.
sentences.zh: 我很想有这样一个开关，这样我默认就会把它打开。

sentences.en: Cause like almost always what I do is I, is I scroll up to the start of the error and I read the error from the start down.
sentences.zh: 因为我几乎总是会滚动到错误信息的开头，然后从上往下读。

sentences.en: Do you need a client format kind of tool for error messages?
sentences.zh: 你需要一个类似 clang-format 的工具来处理报错信息吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I was just thinking that I was thinking I want client format for error messages.
sentences.zh: 我刚才就在想，我想要一个用于报错信息的 clang-format。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That would be cool.
sentences.zh: 那会很酷。

sentences.en: It would be an extremely nice project to write.
sentences.zh: 写这样一个项目会非常棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Somebody, somebody get on that.
sentences.zh: 有人，有人赶紧去搞一个吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: I'm sure there's something out there.
sentences.zh: 我相信市面上肯定已经有类似的东西了。

sentences.en: Um, all right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧。

sentences.en: So after this podcast, there will be.
sentences.zh: 等这期播客结束后，就会有了。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 希望你们喜欢，祝大家度过愉快的一天。
